An infinite board of live pages

A zoomable, pannable canvas where every tile is a working document: notes you can type in, a to-do list, a spreadsheet, a sketch pad, and other pages of this site running in iframes. One drawElementImage() per tile under a zoom transform. The text is re-rasterised at every zoom level, and clicks, focus and typing go to the elements.

Show the code a zoomable board of live tiles
  1. One drawable canvas. The tiles are added to it by script.
  2. Each tile is an element appended to the canvas. A note is a contenteditable, a page is an <iframe>.
  3. Paint: one drawElementImage() per tile, under the camera transform. cam.k is the zoom. Text is drawn again at that zoom, so it stays sharp, and the element's hit box follows the draw. A tile that isn't drawn is parked off stage with updateElementGeometry() so it can't be clicked.
  4. The whole script, with panning, pinch zoom and the minimap.

Drag the background or scroll to pan. Ctrl + wheel or pinch to zoom. Double-click the background for a new note. Drag a tile by its title bar, resize from its corner. Page tiles wake up when you click them; Escape hands the wheel back to the board.

Live checks

ResultExperimentDetail

Findings

  • Zoom is free and sharp. drawElementImage() under a canvas transform replays the element's paint record, so text is re-rasterised at 800% rather than stretched. Hit testing follows the same transform with no extra code.
  • Iframes are tiles like any other. A same-origin iframe inside the canvas paints, takes clicks, typing and wheel scrolling at any zoom, and repaints the board when its own content changes. Other HTML-in-canvas pages, a WebGL scene and this board itself all nest.
  • An iframe swallows input. Wheel and pointer events inside a frame never reach the board, so each page tile has a cover that hands it the pointer only after a click, the way a map embed does.
  • Undrawn doesn't mean unclickable. A tile that is culled or replaced by a placeholder keeps the hit region of its last draw. Park it with updateElementGeometry() or stale tiles catch clicks.
  • Drawing order decides stacking. When tiles overlap, the browser hits the one drawn last. z-index on the elements changes nothing, so bringing a tile to the front means drawing it later, and iframes never have to move in the DOM.
  • Focus can drive the camera. Tab still walks every control on the board in DOM order, so a focusin listener that pans to the focused tile lets the keyboard reach every tile.
  • Semantic zoom is a draw decision. Below a threshold a tile is drawn as a labelled rectangle instead of its DOM. It stays in the document, findable and focusable; focusing it zooms back in.
